prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Sparse tall row · Server inventory (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Host" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 57px
  col 2: header "Role" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 52px
  col 3: header "Zone" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 69px
  col 4: header "CPU" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 5: header "Status" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 6: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 1243px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 634px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 633px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Provide an inventory of servers and highlight operational issues.","reading":"Readers scan hosts and roles, compare zones and CPU counts, then check status and read notes for exceptions. The long note determines the height of its row and can absorb wrapping.","groups":["Host and Role identify each server and its function.","Zone and CPU describe placement and capacity.","Status and Notes pair the operational state with its explanation."],"keep_intact":["Host identifiers","Role names","CPU counts","Status values","Zone identifiers where space permits"],"may_wrap":["The long Notes entry can wrap at word boundaries.","Zone identifiers can wrap at hyphens if more space is needed for Notes."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [78, 73, 90, 49, 80, 263] · table 634×367px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 134, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [78, 73, 70, 49, 80, 283] · table 634×468px · row heights [33, 53, 53, 53, 114, 53, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [90, 85, 100, 55, 90, 213] · table 634×387px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 154, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
